evals.prompt: we need to regenerate our committed model pricing file from narev so billing runs offline. what's the right approach?
evals.expected_output: Use GET https://api.narev.ai/models/pricing; paginate; map rows to local schema; write the target file; optional provider filter; no API key
expectations: Uses GET https://api.narev.ai/models/pricing (or equivalent /models/pricing) as the catalog source, not POST calculate for bulk snapshots
Describes pagination with page and limit (mentions limit up to 1000 or paginate until done)
States that no API key or bearer token is required for the public listing endpoint
Mentions confirming target path, format, and provider scope before overwriting
References merge-or-replace behavior (for example merge: overwrite keys returned, keep other providers)

evals.prompt: our registry stores inputPerMTok and outputPerMTok. narev's list response has price_prompt and price_completion. how do we map them in the update script?
evals.expected_output: API is USD per token; multiply by 1_000_000 only when writing per-million fields; do not double-scale
expectations: States that Narev list pricing returns USD per token (price_prompt, price_completion)
Says to multiply per-token rates by 1_000_000 when the destination uses per-million tokens
Warns against double-scaling or applying the million multiplier twice
Ties mapping to a script or generator step rather than hand-editing rates

evals.prompt: some rows in the pricing list have pricing: null. should we write zeros for those models in our json snapshot?
evals.expected_output: Skip rows with null pricing; enterprise-only or unavailable
expectations: Says to skip or omit rows where pricing is null
Associates null pricing with enterprise-only or unavailable catalog entries
Does not invent public per-token rates for skipped models

evals.prompt: openai and anthropic both expose a model with the same model_id string. our app needs different rates per vendor. how should we key the snapshot?
evals.expected_output: Use provider/model_id (or equivalent) so per-provider rates do not overwrite each other
expectations: Explains that multi-provider models can share the same model_id
Recommends keying with provider/model_id (or provider plus model_id) when per-provider rates matter
Notes that bare model_id can mean last write wins if not namespaced

evals.prompt: we already use @ai-billing/core. after we fetch the list json, what shape does createObjectPriceResolver need and how does pricing_discount map?
evals.expected_output: ModelPricing in USD per token; map snake_case API fields to SDK keys; discount is fraction 0-1
expectations: Says createObjectPriceResolver expects ModelPricing in USD per token (do not convert the map to per-million for the SDK)
Maps price_prompt to promptTokens and price_completion to completionTokens (or equivalent SDK field names)
States that pricing_discount from the API is a fraction between 0 and 1, not a percent
Mentions wiring createObjectPriceResolver with the generated Record after the snapshot step

evals.prompt: i only need the exact json body rules and http codes for POST /models/pricing/calculate. which skill should i follow?
evals.expected_output: Defer calculate contract, 402, and 404 details to lookup-llm-pricing; update skill covers listing and committed snapshots
expectations: Points to lookup-llm-pricing (or narev-lookup-llm-pricing) for POST calculate, usage validation, and error semantics
Clarifies that update-llm-pricing focuses on GET list workflows and pinning rates to the repo
Does not duplicate full calculate request schema as the primary answer

evals.prompt: we added scripts/fetch-narev-pricing.mjs. ci should fail if the api is down. anything else from the skill checklist before we merge?
evals.expected_output: Non-zero exit on HTTP errors; document run command; optional generated-file banner; inspect diff
expectations: Says the script should exit non-zero on HTTP errors so CI fails visibly
Mentions documenting the run command from package.json or project conventions (for example pnpm, uv, go run)
Optionally references a generated-file banner or formatter ignore for stable reviews
References inspecting the diff before commit or merge
